Earlier this month, OpenAI launched its first GPT-6 model and Astra. Now the GPT-6 family has added two new members: GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna.

GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna are now officially available

According to the release notes of the ChatGPT desktop application, GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna consume fewer tokens than the equivalent GPT-5.6 model when running.

GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna will gradually roll out on Codex and ChatGPT Work, with token pricing lower than their previous-generation GPT-5.6 counterparts. Sol is suited for complex coding and agentic workflows; Luna is designed to handle focused, high-volume tasks. Both models will be progressively opened up to Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise and Edu users. Free-tier and Go users will be able to access Luna via the desktop application. Actual availability depends on the rollout schedule and workspace settings; Enterprise administrators will need to enable the new models themselves. Within ChatGPT, the new models will be available on Work and Codex, but not on Chat.

Note the absence of a GPT-6 Terra model this time. It is expected that OpenAI has scrapped its mid-tier offering, choosing to keep only three tiers: Terra (small), Sol (large) and Astra (extra-large).

The following is the official announcement from OpenAI:

Although the most demanding, mission-critical work still calls for the full depth of Astra, work happens at different scales, paces and budgets. That is exactly why we are extending the GPT-6 family with GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna. GPT-6 Astra pioneered a new generation of intelligence — and these two new models carry Astra's intelligence further by raising the cost-efficiency frontier. We trained GPT-6 Sol and Luna using a similar approach to GPT-6 Astra, bringing Astra's state-of-the-art performance in professional work, factual accuracy, coding, computer use and alignment to faster, more economical models.

The company describes the two latest models as not only more capable than the GPT-5.6 versions, but also more affordably priced than Astra (as well as the GPT-5.6 models they replace). Taking the GPT-6 versions of Sol and Luna as an example, they are priced at half the cost of the GPT-5.6 versions.
